claim: "Spalding keeps this Brazilian rhythmic character but adds features from her own jazz background: sophisticated chord extensions, a flexible walking bass line played on the double bass, and passages of wordless scat-style vocal improvisation."
problem: Two errors. (a) On this recording Spalding plays an acoustic bass guitar, not a double bass — confirmed by Pearson's own official Edexcel set-work guide ('The forces used here are simple – female voice, acoustic guitar and acoustic bass guitar... The acoustic bass guitar is a larger version of the acoustic guitar, but with four strings, tuned to E, A, D, G [like the double bass and bass guitar]'). (b) There is no scat singing on this recording: Pearson's guide states the vocal line 'keeps closely to the printed pitches of the score,' with only tempo rubato — it is fully composed and syllabically set to the Portuguese lyric, not wordlessly improvised.
correction: Replace with something like: 'a flexible, virtuosic acoustic bass guitar part, and rubato tempo freedom in the sung vocal line (which stays close to its written melody).' Remove the scat-singing claim.

claim: "A central expressive element of Release is its guest vocal line, sung in the Irish sean-nós tradition... associated with singers such as Iarla Ó Lionaird, who has performed with Afro Celt Sound System."
problem: The officially credited guest vocalist on 'Release' is Sinéad O'Connor — the track is billed 'Afro Celt Sound System feat. Sinéad O'Connor' and album credits list her by name. The lesson never names her anywhere in the unit, pointing only to Iarla Ó Lionáird, who is in fact a founding/core vocalist of Afro Celt Sound System since their first album (1996) — not merely someone 'who has performed with' the band — and whose own vocals appear on this track alongside, not instead of, O'Connor's. A student asked to name the featured guest vocalist on Release would be misled into naming the wrong artist or no artist at all.
correction: Name Sinéad O'Connor as the track's featured/credited guest vocalist. Correct Iarla Ó Lionáird's description to 'the band's regular/founding vocalist' rather than a guest performer; both singers' vocals appear on this track.

claim: "This lesson explores how Esperanza Spalding reworks a 1962 Brazilian bossa nova classic into an intimate jazz fusion built around voice, double bass, guitar and strings."
problem: Per Pearson's official Edexcel set-work guide, the recording uses only three forces: female voice, acoustic guitar and acoustic bass guitar. There is no double bass and no strings/string ensemble anywhere in the piece.
correction: "...built around voice, acoustic bass guitar and acoustic guitar." Remove "strings".

claim: n10: "Spalding's voice paired with her own double bass playing... the double bass — more associated with jazz combos than traditional bossa nova groups"; n15: "a string ensemble is introduced, adding sustained, lush harmonic colour behind the voice, bass and guitar"; n16: "This gradual layering — duet, then guitar, then strings".
problem: (a) The bass instrument on this recording is an acoustic bass guitar, not a double bass — confirmed by Pearson's official guide. (b) There is no string ensemble anywhere in this recording; Pearson's guide lists only voice, acoustic guitar and acoustic bass guitar as the forces used. This 'strings' layer is invented and not supported by any source on this set work.
correction: Replace 'double bass' with 'acoustic bass guitar' throughout. Delete the string-ensemble paragraph and the 'then strings' layering claim — the arrangement adds only one further layer (acoustic guitar), not a second (strings).

claim: Annotated player pin 1: "Voice and bass alone — The duet opening — rubato, intimate, the double bass as the only harmony." Pin 3: "Bass solo — The virtuosic centrepiece — foundation instrument as soloist."
problem: Per Pearson's bar-by-bar structure table, the recording opens with a 3-bar unaccompanied bass introduction (a solo, no voice) before the voice enters at bar 4 — it does not open as a voice-and-bass duet. The one genuinely extended, virtuosic solo passage in the piece is a 34-bar guitar solo (bars 55–88) — by far the longest continuous section in the recording — which this lesson never mentions. The bass's own featured passages (the 3-bar opening and a short link at bars 19–22) are brief by comparison and are not 'the centrepiece'.
correction: Describe the opening as a brief solo acoustic bass guitar introduction, with voice entering shortly after. Identify the guitar solo (not a bass solo) as the recording's extended improvisatory centrepiece, alongside the bass's shorter virtuosic passages.

claim: "Double bass": "A large bowed or plucked string instrument providing the lowest pitched line in jazz ensembles." / "String ensemble": "A group of string instruments, such as violins, violas and cellos, performing together."
problem: Neither instrument is used in this recording. The set work's actual bass instrument is an acoustic bass guitar (confirmed by Pearson's official guide), and there is no string ensemble anywhere in the piece.
correction: Replace the 'Double bass' entry with 'Acoustic bass guitar' (a four-string acoustic instrument tuned like a double bass/bass guitar, played here by Spalding). Remove the 'String ensemble' entry — it does not apply to this set work.

claim: PQ1: "Identify the two instruments that open Spalding's recording of Samba Em Preludio." Mark scheme: "Award 1 mark for correctly naming voice and double bass."
problem: 'Double bass' is the wrong instrument name — Pearson's official guide specifies 'acoustic bass guitar'. A student who studied from this lesson would give the wrong instrument name in the real exam.
correction: Mark scheme should read "...voice and acoustic bass guitar."

claim: KC2: "What texture opens Spalding's recording of Samba Em Preludio?" Correct option: "A duet between voice and double bass."
problem: Wrong instrument name (should be acoustic bass guitar). Also, per Pearson's structure, the true opening bars are a bass-only introduction, not a voice+bass duet.
correction: Correct option should read "A duet between voice and acoustic bass guitar", or be reframed to reflect the brief bass-only opening.

claim: Flashcard 2: "q: What two performers open Spalding's recording in a duet texture? a: Voice and double bass." Flashcard 5: "q: Name two instrumental layers added after the opening duet in Spalding's arrangement. a: Acoustic guitar and string ensemble."
problem: Wrong instrument name (double bass should be acoustic bass guitar); string ensemble is fabricated — no strings feature in this recording.
correction: Flashcard 2 answer: "Voice and acoustic bass guitar." Flashcard 5: the arrangement adds only acoustic guitar as a further layer — remove the string-ensemble answer.

claim: n6: "opens in free time, or rubato, with just voice and double bass"; n7: "an extended, virtuosic double bass solo"; n14 heading: "...the Double Bass as Soloist"; n15: "the piece begins as a duet between voice and double bass"; n16: "The double bass plays a genuinely unusual dual role".
problem: The recording's bass instrument is an acoustic bass guitar, not a double bass — confirmed by Pearson's official Edexcel set-work guide, which explicitly distinguishes the two ('a larger version of the acoustic guitar, but with four strings, tuned...like the double bass and bass guitar' — i.e. tuned similarly to, but a physically different instrument from, the double bass).
correction: Replace 'double bass' with 'acoustic bass guitar' throughout this lesson (heading, prose and pin captions).

claim: n7: "The centrepiece of the recording is an extended, virtuosic double bass solo, where Spalding improvises over the harmonic pattern established earlier"; n15: "the piece begins as a duet between voice and double bass — a thin, exposed texture".
problem: Per Pearson's bar-by-bar structure, the piece opens with a 3-bar solo bass introduction (no voice), not a duet, and the genuinely extended solo passage is a 34-bar guitar solo (bars 55–88) — the longest continuous section of the piece — which this lesson omits entirely. The bass's own featured passages (opening introduction + a short link) are brief by comparison.
correction: Describe the opening as a brief unaccompanied bass introduction before the voice enters, and identify the guitar solo as the recording's extended improvisatory centrepiece.

claim: PQ1: "Name the two performers/instruments heard in the opening rubato section of Samba Em Preludio." Mark scheme: "Award 1 mark for correctly identifying voice and double bass." PQ3: "Explain how the double bass functions in two different roles across the recording."
problem: Wrong instrument name throughout — should be acoustic bass guitar, per Pearson's official set-work guide.
correction: Replace 'double bass' with 'acoustic bass guitar' in both the question text and mark scheme.

claim: KC2: "What instrument does Esperanza Spalding play and sing simultaneously on this recording?" Correct option: "Double bass." KC3: "How does the piece begin?" Correct option: "In free time (rubato) as a duet."
problem: KC2's correct answer names the wrong instrument (should be acoustic bass guitar). KC3's correct answer overstates the very opening: Pearson's structure shows the piece opening with an unaccompanied bass introduction (bars 1–3) before the voice enters at bar 4.
correction: KC2 correct option should read "Acoustic bass guitar." KC3 should reflect a brief solo-bass introduction preceding the voice's entry, rather than an immediate duet.

claim: Flashcard 2: "a: An extended, virtuosic double bass solo played by Esperanza Spalding over the established harmony." Flashcard 3: "q: What two roles does the double bass play across the piece?"
problem: Wrong instrument name; also the 'centrepiece' solo is more accurately the 34-bar guitar solo, not an extended bass solo.
correction: Replace 'double bass' with 'acoustic bass guitar'; consider reframing flashcard 2 to credit the guitar solo as the recording's main extended solo passage.

problem: The recording is from Spalding's 2008 album 'Esperanza', not 2010. This caption contradicts the lesson's own correctly-dated prose elsewhere in the unit (L1 and L5 both correctly say '2008 album Esperanza') and Pearson's official set-work guide.
correction: Change the caption year to (2008). Same fix needed in Lesson 5's identical caption.
